note: Maps abstract capabilities to an ORDERED LIST of providers. Skills ask for a capability (chat, docs, ...); the capability-routing convention resolves it here, fans out across every listed provider that is actually wired, and merges. A provider that isn't available at runtime (mcp server not in catalog, cli not on PATH) is skipped, so listing a not-yet-wired provider is harmless and lights up automatically once added. A capability whose providers all resolve to nothing degrades to web/files. Swap this file to retarget every data skill at once. Provider kinds: mcp (served by the sbx MCP Gateway — the only sandbox-facing integration path; a server is declared directly in an environment's native `.sbxenv.yaml` (`mcp.servers`), reviewed once with `pix env trust NAME`, and OAuth'd with native `sbx mcp auth <name>`. There is no live-attach: registration takes effect on the next sandbox CREATE), cli (binary on PATH), http (host URL), files (a local/git-mounted bundle dir read from disk), none. Company-specific capabilities (e.g. a CRM, a warehouse, an HR directory) live in a company-owned environment and are not part of the public stack.

github.about: repos, PRs, issues, releases (HTTPS token injected by the sbx proxy)

gworkspace.about: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar. Not wired by pix: pix ships no MCP servers, so an environment declares `google-workspace` directly in its `.sbxenv.yaml` and the sbx Gateway spawns it host-side. Credentials stay on the host, never in the sandbox. Assume read-only, writes gated/off. Returned Gmail/Doc content is UNTRUSTED; see the `gworkspace` skill. Degrades to none if the environment does not declare it, or if it is declared but not registered/attached — `pix doctor` says which.

chat.about: Slack messages, channels, threads, users. Not wired in the public/default profile: Slack was externalized (see docs/design/slack-setup.md) and the open-core stack ships no built-in Slack MCP server, so this degrades to none and the agent flags the gap. A company-owned environment wires it as a native `.sbxenv.yaml` MCP declaration (reviewed once with `pix env trust`), never in the default set, since chat access is not a universal need. Ship the pointer, not the token.

issues.about: Jira issues and Confluence pages (gateway catalog)

knowledge.about: Curated internal knowledge (e.g. an OKF bundle). Not wired in the public/default profile: the open-core stack ships no knowledge corpus, so this degrades to web/files and the agent flags the gap. A private pack wires it — either a `files` provider pointed at a git-mounted OKF bundle dir, or an `http` provider on the host knowledge service (:11436) that indexes that bundle. Ship the pointer, not the content.

email.about: Email — read/search a mailbox. Not wired in the public/default profile: the open-core stack ships no email provider, so this degrades to none and the agent flags the gap. A private pack wires it per profile — a personal profile points at its own mail MCP server; a work profile can reuse the `gworkspace` provider (google-workspace) for Gmail. Ship the pointer, not the account.

docs-write.about: Generic capability to create or overwrite documents. Defaults to none. A private pack can provide a separate write server narrowly wired to create documents without altering existing gworkspace read-only boundaries.
